title: Phase 2 dashboard launched
detail: The v1 prototype was split into a modular Next.js app. All numbers are read from CSV files in data/.

title: CSV files instead of a database for now
detail: The data is small, updated at most daily and written by one pipeline. Git history gives an audit trail. Supabase is deferred until logins or saved simulations are needed (roadmap Batch 9).

title: Every data row is labelled real or illustrative
detail: Each row carries an is_illustrative flag. While any displayed row is a placeholder, the header shows a warning that links to the methodology page.

title: Bad data stops the build
detail: A missing column, an out-of-range score or an unknown tier now fails the build and names the file and line, so a wrong number never goes live.

title: NOAA CO2 ingest script added
detail: scripts/ingest_co2.py downloads Mauna Loa monthly CO2 into data/indicators.csv as raw values. It has not been run yet.

title: Headline survival probability removed
detail: The 68.4% figure was a placeholder with no model behind it. It was replaced by a ranked Top Bottlenecks panel. A survival estimate returns only with a published model and uncertainty bands (roadmap Batch 5).

title: Survival trend chart replaced
detail: The historical and projected survival chart was removed with the headline number. A Tier Scores Over Time chart shows all four tiers on one timeline instead.

title: Methodology page added
detail: Shows where every number comes from, how it is made and whether it is real. Generated from the data files, so it cannot drift from what is displayed.

title: Site-wide navigation
detail: Header, navigation and footer moved into the shared layout so every page gets them. Planned pages appear greyed out with their roadmap batch.

title: Change log page added
detail: This page. Hand-written entries for site and method changes; ingest scripts add an entry automatically whenever they change data.

title: Design tokens
detail: All colours now come from one file, lib/tokens.ts, used by both the page styles and the charts. Shared panel, card, heading and label styles keep every page consistent. Changing one value restyles the whole site.

title: Ingest runner with 5 Existential sources
detail: scripts/ingest.py replaces the CO2-only script. Sources: NOAA CO2 (Mauna Loa), NOAA methane and nitrous oxide (global), NASA GISTEMP global temperature anomaly, and FAS nuclear warhead stockpiles via Our World in Data. Every source gets the same range, row-count and shrink checks. Not yet run.

title: Measured Indicators panel
detail: New dashboard panel showing real, downloaded indicators by tier: latest value, 1-year and 10-year change, a 30-year sparkline and a source link. Each card is marked Real or Illustrative from the data file. Shows a waiting state until the first ingest run.

title: 10 more sources across three tiers
detail: Added to scripts/ingest.py: extreme poverty, undernourishment and conflict deaths (Systemic); internet use, low-carbon electricity, solar module price and generative-AI investment (Tech); life expectancy, child mortality and the Human Development Index (Flourishing). All are world totals from Our World in Data. Not yet run; a few may need a fix on the first real download.

title: Official targets on indicator cards
detail: Each Measured Indicators card now shows its official target where one exists: World Bank poverty below 3% by 2030, UN goals for hunger, child mortality and internet access, the Paris 1.5 °C limit and the nuclear ban treaty's goal of zero warheads. Where no official target exists, the card says which direction is better instead of inventing one. Large numbers are now shortened (e.g. 143.8B).

title: Real tier scores (method v1)
detail: The four tier scores are now computed from the 15 real indicators instead of placeholders. Each indicator is scored 0-100: progress toward its official target, headroom under a limit, or, where no target exists, its position between the worst and best values on record. A tier is the plain average of its indicators. Top Bottlenecks now lists the five lowest-scoring indicators. The Illustrative data warning is removed because nothing shown is a placeholder any more. Known limits are listed on the Methodology page.

title: Trend scoring for indicators without targets (method v2)
detail: Indicators with no official target (greenhouse gases, conflict deaths, life expectancy, HDI, low-carbon power, solar price) are now scored on their 10-year trend instead of their position in their own record. 50 means flat; each 1% change in the better direction adds 5 points. v1 pinned steadily rising series near 0 or 100, which pushed Existential down and Flourishing up.

title: 5 more sources (20 total)
detail: Added: near-Earth asteroid detection (Existential, first non-climate risk alongside warheads; target from the 2005 US NEO Survey Act), the Living Planet Index (Systemic), electricity access (Tech), clean-cooking access and DTP3 vaccination coverage (Flourishing). Each comes with its official target where one exists.

detail: Latest reading 2025: 11501 asteroids (NASA Center for Near-Earth Object Studies via Our World in Data). History now 36 years.

detail: Latest reading 2024: 91.93 % of population (World Bank (SDG 7.1.1) via Our World in Data). History now 27 years.

detail: Latest reading 2024: 75.00 % of population (WHO (SDG 7.1.2) via World Bank and Our World in Data). History now 25 years.

detail: Latest reading 2025: 85.0 % of one-year-olds (WHO and UNICEF via Our World in Data). History now 46 years.

detail: Latest reading 2022: 0.268 index (1970 = 1) (WWF and Zoological Society of London via Our World in Data). History now 53 years.

title: Uncertainty range on tier scores
detail: Each tier card now shows a low-high range: the tier score recomputed with a 5, 10 or 15-year trend window, 2.5, 5 or 10 points per 1% change, and with each indicator left out in turn. It shows how much a score depends on method choices, not measurement error in the data.

title: Levers page
detail: New page listing what would move each indicator and who can act on it, worst score first. Covers the 11 lowest-scoring indicators, including conflict deaths, vaccination, hunger, temperature, greenhouse gases, wildlife populations, clean cooking, electricity access and asteroid detection. Each lever names its source (an agreed international target or published evidence); Earth OS does not rate governments itself.

title: Tier renamed: Tech Governance is now Clean Tech & Access
detail: The tier measures how widely clean electricity, cheap solar, power at home and internet access are spreading, not whether technology such as AI is well governed. The new name says what it measures. Scores are unchanged.

title: Tier card charts use a fixed 0-100 scale
detail: The small charts on each tier card used to zoom in on their own range, so a change from 20 to 21 looked like a steep climb. They now use the same 0-100 scale as the scores, so the height of a bar or line matches the real size of the change.

title: Policies page (climate)
detail: New page showing Climate Action Tracker ratings for the 10 largest emitters, worst first, each with its rating date and a link to the source. None is rated on track for 2 °C. Earth OS shows the tracker's ratings as published and does not rate countries itself.

title: Country gameplans on the Policies page
detail: Each country on the Policies page now opens its own page with a step-by-step gameplan to get on track, summarised from the Climate Action Tracker's recommendations. Added a Closest to on track row (The Gambia, Philippines, Chile, all rated Almost sufficient) and refreshed rating dates for China, India, Saudi Arabia and Canada.

title: Master gameplan and policy topics
detail: The Policies page now opens with a master gameplan: the 11 shared steps every country plan is built from, ranked by how many countries need each, with links to each country. Each step on a country page is tagged with its master step. The page title is now a topic menu; Climate is live and Nuclear weapons, Nature, Food, Health and AI governance are planned.

title: Emissions share on the Policies page
detail: Each country now shows its share of world greenhouse gas emissions for 2025 (EDGAR, EU Joint Research Centre, excluding land use). The master gameplan is now ranked by impact (the share of world emissions from the countries that still need each step) instead of by country count, and the page notes that the 10 largest emitters produce about 69% of the total. The master gameplan can also be minimised with a +/- button.

title: Matrix and country views for the master gameplan
detail: The master gameplan now has three views: List, Matrix and By country. The matrix shows every step against every country, with each column as wide as that country's share of world emissions, so you can see at a glance who still needs to do what. By country flips it: each country, biggest emitter first, with the steps it still needs.

title: Proper tier names on the Levers page
detail: Each lever group now shows its tier by full name (for example Systemic Health) instead of the short internal label.

title: Nuclear weapons on the Policies page
detail: New Nuclear weapons topic covering the nine nuclear-armed countries. Each shows its Nuclear Threat Initiative security score (2026), change since 2023 and rank, plus SIPRI's estimate of its warhead stockpile. The Nuclear Weapons Ban Monitor places all nine as opposed to the UN nuclear ban treaty.

title: Impact section on the Nuclear weapons topic
detail: Nuclear weapons now has an Impact panel: why it matters, the worst case, the effect on humanity's survival, the best case, where experts disagree, knock-on effects and a dated timeline. Every line shows its source and whether it is measured, modelled or an expert judgement. Earth OS adds no estimates of its own.

title: Impact and Master gameplan panels can be minimised
detail: The Impact panel on Nuclear weapons now has a +/- button to minimise or open it, like the Master gameplan. A Master gameplan placeholder sits in the same position on the Nuclear page so the layout matches Climate.

title: Impact section on the Climate topic
detail: Climate now has an Impact panel in the same place as Nuclear weapons: why it matters, the worst case, the effect on humanity's survival, the best case, where experts disagree, knock-on effects, who is affected and a dated timeline. Every line shows its source and whether it is measured, modelled or an expert judgement.

title: Clickable steps in the Climate master gameplan
detail: Master gameplan steps can now open their own page with a plain-language explanation, concrete sourced steps and the countries that still need to do it. Phase out coal is first; the other steps follow. Every line shows its source and confidence label.

title: Detailed steps for Stop fossil fuel expansion
detail: The top step of the Climate master gameplan now opens its own page: a plain-language explanation, five sourced steps to achieve it and the countries that still need to take it. Every line shows its source and confidence label.

title: Detailed steps for Scale up clean power
detail: The Scale up clean power step now opens its own page: a plain-language explanation, five sourced steps to achieve it and the countries that still need to take it. Every line shows its source and confidence label.

title: Dashboard tooltip no longer hidden
detail: The info tooltip on each score card (for example Existential Survival) was cut off by the card next to it. The card you hover now sits on top, so the whole note is readable.

title: Dashboard tooltip fits inside its card
detail: The info note on the score cards ran off the right edge of the screen on the last card. It now sits inside its own card, so the whole note is readable on every card.

title: Detailed steps for Make carbon prices bite
detail: The Make carbon prices bite step now opens its own page: a plain-language explanation, five sourced steps to achieve it and the countries that still need to take it. Every line shows its source and confidence label.

title: Clearer title for the carbon price step
detail: The Climate master gameplan step "Make carbon prices bite" is now called "Put a real price on carbon".

title: Detailed steps for the methane step
detail: Methane step page now lists plain-words lines, how-to steps and who needs to act, each with a source and confidence label.

title: Detailed steps for six more master steps
detail: Industry, targets, electrify, finance, plan and land step pages now carry plain-words lines and how-to steps with named sources and confidence labels.

title: Separate target and action ratings for 13 countries
detail: Country cards now show the Climate Action Tracker's separate rating of each country's target (against fair share) and of its policies and action, next to the overall rating.

title: Farm methane added to the methane step
detail: Four new sourced lines on livestock, rice and farm methane, from UNEP, FAO and the Clean Air Task Force.

title: Nuclear weapons: master gameplan and country gameplans
detail: Seven master steps, each with its own page, and a gameplan for each of the nine nuclear-armed countries. Every line has a source and a confidence label; no ranking or impact estimate is added.

title: Nature & biodiversity topic
detail: New Policies topic. Ratings are the Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026 Biodiversity & Habitat score for the 17 megadiverse countries the UN lists (Venezuela is not scored by the index, so 16 are shown). It has an Impact panel, a five-step master gameplan with a page per step, and a gameplan per country built from each country's weakest EPI indicators. Every line has a source and a confidence label; no ranking or impact estimate is added.

title: Food & hunger topic
detail: New Policies topic. Ratings are the 2026 Global Hunger Index score for the 15 countries with the highest published scores (four more countries have only a provisional hunger category and no score). It has an Impact panel, a five-step master gameplan with a page per step, and a gameplan per country built from each country's weakest hunger indicators. Every line has a source and a confidence label; no ranking or impact estimate is added.

title: Food & hunger review fixes
detail: Scores and measures now always show one decimal (for example 47.0). Step names and wording made the same on every page. The Impact panel now says the 35.5 million acutely malnourished children are in the food-crisis countries the report covers, so it no longer looks like it contradicts the global figure on the wasting step page. Fixed a rounding difference for Madagascar, Haiti and the Central African Republic, where the gameplan text showed undernourishment 0.1 lower than the bar.

title: Health & vaccination topic
detail: New Policies topic. Ratings are the WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for 2025, released 15 July 2026, for the 15 countries with the lowest third-dose DTP coverage. It has an Impact panel, a five-step master gameplan with a page per step, and a gameplan per country that lists its four coverage measures lowest first, then funding and data. Every line has a source and a confidence label; no ranking or impact estimate is added.

title: Health & vaccination review fixes
detail: Step pages now name the measure correctly (for example "first-dose DTP"). Data notes on the Kazakhstan, Afghanistan, Central African Republic and Gabon cards now name their source.

title: Health & vaccination cross-check
detail: Cross-checked against the WHO/UNICEF 2025 technical notes. For 12 of the 15 countries the estimate is well below government-reported coverage; each card now gives the reported figure and the reason WHO and UNICEF give. Central African Republic and Gabon are now described as not having introduced the second measles dose, which is why their estimate is 0%.

title: AI governance topic added
detail: New Policies topic: responsible AI governance scores from the Global Index on Responsible AI (GIRAI) 2026 for the 15 leading AI countries in the Stanford HAI Global AI Vibrancy ranking that GIRAI assesses (Luxembourg is not assessed, so Brazil is included). Five master gameplan steps, one per GIRAI dimension; country gameplans list dimensions lowest score first. Impact panel with 21 sourced lines. Figures checked against the GIRAI country pages and press coverage (US 53.34, #27).

title: AI governance review and cross-check
detail: All 15 countries' scores and the 75 gameplan lines re-checked against the GIRAI country table: no mismatches. Added a note to South Korea: GIRAI evidence runs to September 2025, so the AI Basic Act (in force January 2026) is not counted. Two "how to achieve it" lines reworded or removed where the source did not say exactly that.

title: Tidy-up, nuclear steps and consistency check
detail: Removed the four retired placeholder files (placeholder tier scores and bottlenecks, the old survival number and its trend) from data/ and from the Methodology page; the dashboard now refuses to build without real indicator data instead of falling back to placeholders. Nuclear: a risk-reduction step added for India, Pakistan and North Korea, with two sourced lines on the step page. Consistency check across all six topics: every line has a source, link and confidence label; no structural problems. One health source swapped from a news mirror to the WHO/UNICEF/Gavi release.

title: Readiness radar and "Moving the Wrong Way" alerts
detail: Dashboard: a radar chart of the four tier scores with their low-high range, and a list of the indicators whose score fell most over the latest year (each year scored with only the data published by then, same method v2). Roadmap B4 (ideas I1, I2).

title: Uncertainty bands for every year
detail: The low-high range (same method variants as before: trend window, points per 1% change, leave one indicator out) is now worked out for every year, not just the latest, and drawn as a thin bar on each tier card chart. It still measures how much a score depends on scoring choices, not measurement error in the sources; that question is in the outside review brief (Review 1). Roadmap B3.

title: New tier colours; tier cards removed
detail: Tier colours changed from red, amber, green to blue (Existential Survival), teal (Systemic Health), purple (Clean Tech & Access) and magenta (Human Flourishing), so tier colours no longer read as good or bad; red, amber and yellow stay only for severity. The four tier cards were removed because Tier Scores Over Time already shows the same history; its legend now carries each tier's score, range and status.

title: Site renamed to EarthOS
detail: The site title changed from Global Survival Matrix to EarthOS, with the subtitle Humanity's vital signs (previously The Humanity Project), in the header, browser tab and footer.

title: Israel risk-reduction step; EarthOS name across pages
detail: Added a sourced risk-reduction step for Israel (a direct crisis channel with Iran), with two new context lines (Washington Post, Israel Hayom). Every page title and note now uses the EarthOS name.

title: CO2 updated: 1 new month, 10 revised by the source
detail: Latest reading 2026-10: 426.69 ppm (NOAA GML Mauna Loa monthly mean CO2). History now 824 months.

title: Methane updated: 2 new months, 431 revised by the source
detail: Latest reading 2026-08: 1936.37 ppb (NOAA GML global monthly mean CH4). History now 518 months.

title: Nitrous oxide updated: 2 new months, 19 revised by the source
detail: Latest reading 2026-08: 340.02 ppb (NOAA GML global monthly mean N2O). History now 308 months.

title: Forecasts page (expert estimates)
detail: New Forecasts page: published estimates of extinction, global catastrophe and existential catastrophe (Forecasting Research Institute tournament, Toby Ord, Metaculus) shown side by side on a log scale, never averaged. EarthOS publishes no survival percentage of its own. Methodology principle updated to match.

title: Projections tested and not published
detail: Three projection methods were tested on past data against pass marks set in advance (85-95% of outcomes inside the 90% band, 40-60% inside the 50% band). None passed: method 1 54% and 29%, method 2 51% and 29%, method 3 85% and 32% at 10 years and 80% and 33% at 5 years. No projections are published; the Forecasts page reports the tests.

title: Long-range scenarios on the Forecasts page
detail: Added published scenarios, labelled modelled: IPCC AR6 warming by 2081-2100 under five emissions scenarios, UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 warming this century under current policies, pledges, and pledges plus net-zero targets, and the UN World Population Prospects 2024 life expectancy projection for 2054. Today's measured value is marked on each chart.

title: New look (design direction B)
detail: Site restyled in the "Night observatory" direction chosen on 22 Nov: deep navy background, Space Grotesk headings, Inter text, numbers in JetBrains Mono, calmer cards and sentence-case labels. A switch in the header turns on a light version; the choice is remembered in the browser.

title: Clearer topic dropdown on Policies
detail: The topic picker on Policies pages is now a standard labelled Topic dropdown above the title, instead of a small arrow beside the title that was easy to miss.

title: Shorter Policies pages
detail: All six Policies topics use a new layout: the topic dropdown and key numbers (each with its source and confidence label) sit in a side column; the header is a question and one summary line; countries are a compact list with bars instead of cards; the gameplan is step cards, first six shown; Impact is folded into rows that open on click. Longer explanations moved to the info tip and a Sources and notes section. No figures changed.

title: Dashboard in the new layout
detail: The Dashboard now opens with the four area scores as large tiles beside the scores-over-time chart. Weakest points open on tap to say what each measures; Moving the wrong way shows the largest fall big and the rest as a short list; a new card shows the spread of published expert extinction estimates for 2100 and links to Forecasts. The readiness radar was removed because the tiles show the same scores. Also on Policies: tidier list spacing and "1 country" wording. No figures changed.

title: Levers, Forecasts, Methodology and Change log in the new layout
detail: Each page now opens with a plain title and one summary line. Levers shows the four weakest indicators first, with the evidence behind each lever one tap away. Forecasts leads with the extinction range; other definitions, how to read the numbers, the projection tests and sources fold away. Methodology shows six short rules and the scoring method and data files as rows that open on tap. The change log is a compact list; tap a change for the reason. No figures changed.

title: Methodology lists every data file
detail: The Data files section on Methodology now lists all 23 files the site is built from, grouped by Dashboard, Policies, Forecasts and Site, each with what it feeds, how it is made and its sources. It listed only 4 before. The build now fails if a new data file is added without a description.

title: Quality check: phone layout, links and readability
detail: On phones the menu no longer shows a scroll bar and the light/dark switch stays beside the logo. Policy pages show the title before the key numbers on small screens. All 168 outside source links were checked: one broken Yale EPI link on Nature was replaced with the current 2026 page; 44 others are behind bot protection and could not be checked automatically. Very light grey text was darkened to meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum. No figures changed.

title: Security check
detail: Checked the site for known security problems. Next.js 16.4.6 and React 19.3.1 already include every published security fix, and the site uses none of the features those fixes covered. No secrets are uploaded, and all outside links open safely. Added browser security headers (content security policy, no framing, HTTPS only), locked every software package to an exact version, and stopped uploading working folders that the site does not use. No figures changed.

title: New page: The Brief
detail: A short, editorial read on the latest numbers: the four area scores, the largest fall this year, the three weakest indicators with one lever each, the biggest 10-year gains, one key number per policy topic and the expert extinction range. It is written from the same data files as the dashboard, so it updates whenever the data does, and it can be printed or saved as a PDF. A monthly email edition on Substack will follow. No figures changed.
affects: app/report/page.tsx, components/report/PrintButton.tsx, components/report/SubscribeBox.tsx, lib/site.ts, lib/nav.ts, lib/tokens.ts, app/page.tsx

title: Brief: sign up by email
detail: The Brief now has a Subscribe button that opens the newsletter on Substack (joeldsouza3.substack.com). Sign-up happens on Substack, so EarthOS itself collects no email addresses. No figures changed.

title: Brief: why EarthOS exists
detail: The Brief now opens with the project's purpose: we all share one goal, survival, and EarthOS shows the whole picture so people can agree on where we stand and focus on what would help. It cites the estimate that more than 99% of species that ever lived are extinct (National Geographic). No figures changed.

title: New page: What if
detail: Pick a choice the world could make, such as every country meeting its climate pledge, and see where published models say it leads, why, and who can act. Six cards: climate pledges (UNEP), the energy system (IEA), child survival (UN IGME), vaccines (WHO), nature (Leclère et al., Nature 2020) and the hunger trend (SOFI 2026). EarthOS computes nothing here: each card switches only between scenarios from one source and one model, and the build fails if a card mixes sources. No figures on other pages changed.
affects: app/what-if/page.tsx, components/whatif/WhatIfCard.tsx, lib/whatif.ts, data/whatif.csv, lib/methodology.ts, lib/nav.ts

title: New page: Solved
detail: Proof that global problems can be solved: smallpox (eradicated 1980), the ozone hole (nearly 99% of harmful chemicals phased out), leaded petrol (gone since 2021), polio (down more than 99%) and nuclear stockpiles (down from about 70,300 to about 12,187, but rising again). Each shows how it was done and its source. A second section sorts problems by the kind of cooperation they need, after economist Scott Barrett, labelled as expert judgement. No figures on other pages changed.

title: Data now checked automatically every month
detail: All 20 sources are now downloaded and checked automatically on the 2nd of each month, on GitHub. The site is rebuilt only if every file passes its checks. The footer of every page and the Dashboard now show when the data was last checked and when the next check is due. A source that cannot be reached keeps its previous numbers and is flagged on the Dashboard.

title: New page: Use the data
detail: Every indicator can now be shared or embedded: a live card for websites, a share link that shows the card as a picture on LinkedIn and other social sites, and a downloadable image. Each Dashboard card has a Share link. The same page offers free downloads: the latest values of all 20 indicators and the four area scores (JSON), the full history of every indicator (CSV), and one indicator at a time (JSON). Measured values keep their source links and their publishers' terms.

title: New page: Track record
detail: Under Forecasts, a page that sets six well-known past forecasts against what then happened: the IPCC's 1990 warming rate, the UN's 1958 population figure for 2000, President Kennedy's 1963 nuclear warning, the 1980 Ehrlich-Simon wager, and two questions from the forecasting tournament whose extinction estimates are on the Forecasts page. Two were close, two too high, one too low and one went the wrong way. Each verdict comes from a fixed rule that the build re-checks, and each outcome from a separate named source. A seventh candidate, on solar power, was left out because its source could not be opened to verify.

title: Track record: Coming due
detail: The Track record page now lists five published forecasts whose date has not arrived: the WMO's 70% chance that 2025 to 2029 averages more than 1.5 °C, and current-trend forecasts for 2030 of extreme poverty (8.9%), hunger (510 to 520 million people), people without electricity (at least 644 million) and clean cooking (78%). Each shows its source and, where EarthOS tracks the same thing, the live figure. When a date passes and the result is published, the forecast moves to the checked list with its verdict.

title: New page: Deep time
detail: Under Forecasts, a page on whether history can warn us in time. It shows six published methods that claim to spot crises early, from a 2010 forecast of rising unrest to warning signs found in Stone Age population records, each with how it was tested and what the tests found. Three were tested on what happened after they were published, one on held-back data, and two only on the past they were built from. One that looked strong weakened when re-tested on later years. EarthOS runs no test of its own here and gives no overall score.

title: Deep time: the long view
detail: The Deep time page now sets three measures against long published records: carbon dioxide in the air over 800,000 years from Antarctic ice cores, global temperature over 2,000 years from the PAGES 2k reconstruction, and world population over 12,000 years. Reconstructed stretches are drawn apart from the measured record and labelled, and a shaded strip shows how much of each history the dashboard's own chart covers. The live Mauna Loa CO2 line updates with the monthly refresh; the reconstructions are fixed history.

title: Scoring method v3: greenhouse gases counted once
detail: Carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide are now averaged into one greenhouse-gas item before the Existential Survival score is worked out, so that tier weighs temperature, greenhouse gases, nuclear weapons and asteroids equally. Before, the three gases plus temperature made up four of its six items. The tier score rises from 34.2 to 38.7 (range 21.8 to 43.5 becomes 24.1 to 50.8) because the gases score low and now carry less weight; no measurement changed. The other three tiers are unchanged. The suggestion came from an outside review.

title: Clearer cards and a shorter menu
detail: Fixes from an outside review: the temperature card now says its headline figure is against NASA's 1951-1980 average while the 1.5 °C bar uses 1880-1900 as pre-industrial; Weakest points shows the actual figure under each score, so a 0 for vaccination reads as 85% coverage, below its 2019 level; the hunger card notes the UN's 2026 figures (7.8% in 2025, with 2024 revised to 8.1%) until the data feed catches up; the nuclear card notes that warheads available for use are rising again while the total falls; older yearly figures say "latest published"; card counts say data points rather than years; the header keeps seven main pages with Data, Methodology and Change log under More; and the home page has a link to subscribe to the monthly Brief.

title: New page: Funding
detail: Under More, a page on what it costs to close the gap in five areas: clean energy (about $2.2 trillion expected in 2026 against around $4.5 trillion a year needed by the early 2030s), childhood vaccination (over $9 billion secured of Gavi's $11.9 billion for 2026 to 2030), hunger (an extra $33 to $50 billion a year, from two models), nature ($220 billion in 2023 against $571 billion a year needed by 2030) and asteroid detection (funded, with no published gap). Each figure is labelled and sourced, each card says what stands in the way besides money, and the areas are never added together. Military spending and fossil fuel subsidies are shown alongside for scale.

title: The Brief: monthly archive
detail: Each monthly data refresh now saves that month's Brief, and the Brief page has a Century, Year and Month picker to open past issues. Archived issues show the numbers as they stood that month, with a note that sources may have revised them since. The archive starts with November 2026. The refresh also checks every source link each month and lists any broken ones in its run report.

title: Broken source links fixed
detail: The first monthly link check found two dead source links, now replaced: the IPCC's 1990 summary on the Track record page now links to the IPCC's current page for that report, and a news report on the UN biodiversity progress report now links to the Convention on Biological Diversity's own press release (one sentence was reworded to match what the release says). Links to three sites that refuse automated checks but work in a browser are now reported as blocked, not broken.

title: Menu reordered as a story
detail: The main menu now runs in story order: Dashboard (where we are), Forecasts (where we are heading), Policies (what governments are doing), What if (what published scenarios say if we change course), Funding (what it costs), Solved (proof it can be done) and Brief (the monthly summary). Levers moves under More, with links to it kept on Weakest points and on each Funding card. Each of these pages now ends with a link to the next one, and the Brief links back to the start. The temperature card's target line now says its 1.46 °C is a 12-month average.

title: New page: Not covered yet
detail: A new page lists five areas EarthOS does not cover in depth yet: pandemic preparedness, clean water and sanitation, plastic pollution, drug-resistant infections and ocean protection. Each shows one sourced headline number, labelled measured or modelled, and a sourced line on where things stand. They are not scored and change no other page. It is under More, and linked from the Policies topic pages and the Funding page.

title: Weakest points show the score scale
detail: Each score in Weakest points now reads as out of 100 (for example 0/100), so the scale is clear without opening the info button.

title: Forecasts moves after Funding
detail: The main menu, footer and Next links now run Dashboard, Policies, What if, Funding, Forecasts, Solved, Brief. Levers, Not covered yet, Data, Methodology and Change log stay under More.

title: Temperature description restored
detail: A formatting error in indicator_info.csv had cut the Global temperature rise description after its first clause, hiding the explanation of its two baselines (NASA's 1951-1980 average for the headline figure, 1880-1900 for the 1.5 °C bar). The full text now shows on the card and in Weakest points, and the build now refuses any data row with an unquoted comma.

title: Clearer charts on Forecasts
detail: The risk charts now put superforecasters and domain experts from the same tournament on one line per cause, so the gap between them shows; the figures are unchanged and nothing is averaged. Each chart's scale now fits its own figures and adds plain 1-in-N labels; this also fixes range bars that ran off the left edge of the existential-risk chart. The temperature scenarios show the Paris Agreement range (1.5 to 2 °C) behind every row, with a count of how many published scenarios end above it. Life expectancy is now a line of the measured record since 1900 leading to the UN's projection for 2054.

title: Sources checked for newer editions
detail: Every source on the site was checked against its publisher for a newer edition. Updated: the Forecasts page adds the Forecasting Research Institute's mid-2026 panel (global catastrophe, all causes and AI) beside its 2022 tournament, and a 2024 survey of 1,580 AI researchers; each row now shows the year people were asked. The AI policy page adds both. Coming due: WMO's 2026 update (75% chance that 2026 to 2030 averages above 1.5 °C, was 70% for 2025 to 2029), the UN's 2026 poverty projection (about 9% in 2030, was 8.9%) and the 2026 clean-cooking projection (79%, was 78%). Climate: COP31 ended on 22 November without a main agreement; coal demand figures now come from the IEA's 2026 mid-year update; net-zero figures from the 2026 Net Zero Stocktake. Nature: Planetary Health Check 2026. Hunger funding: the upper estimate is now ZEF's 2024 figure of $93 billion a year (was $50 billion from 2020). Vaccines: the 2024 pace from WHO's mid-term review (4.3 million deaths averted, was 4.2 million for 2023). Plastics: next treaty round set for March 2027. Checked and still the latest edition: the 2022 tournament's extinction figures, Toby Ord (2020), IPCC AR6 (2021), UN World Population Prospects 2024 (next edition moved to 2027), the OECD plastics figures, the WHO measles report (November 2025) and the 2022 ozone assessment (the 2026 one is in preparation).

title: Promises page and a guide for reusing the format
detail: New Promises page (under More): 16 public commitments beside the measured figure. Nine have a deadline ahead (five Sustainable Development Goal targets, vaccination, protecting 30% of land and sea, tripling renewables, halting forest loss), four have no end date (the Paris Agreement, nuclear disarmament, 0.7% aid, the ozone treaty) and three are past their deadline (the $100 billion climate finance goal and two Millennium Development Goals). EarthOS gives no verdict before a deadline; results for past deadlines are the named source's finding. Also new: a guide in the repo for anyone who wants to use the format for a city, state or country (docs/use-this-for-your-city.md), linked from the footer. The code is MIT-licensed.

title: Priorities page: six ways to rank the same problems
detail: New Priorities page (under More). It takes a fixed list of 12 problems and ranks it six ways, each from a named source: deaths a year now, people living with it now, risk to humanity's future (Toby Ord, 2020), a 10-year expert survey (World Economic Forum, 2026), benefit per dollar (Copenhagen Consensus, 2023) and public worry (Ipsos, October 2026). The six lenses put six different problems first. EarthOS publishes no combined ranking: readers set their own weights, and each problem shows in how many lenses it is in the top three. Every lens carries two checks, coverage (how many of the 12 problems it can rank) and stability (how many pairs keep their order if the figures are off by 25%, or by the range the source itself states). Where a lens has no figure for a problem, the page says why. Not done yet: a look back at whether any lens would have pointed at the problems that later did the most harm.

title: Priorities: thin evidence is pulled toward the middle
detail: In a reader's own ranking on the Priorities page, a problem that fewer than three of the weighted lenses have a figure for now has its score topped up to three with neutral scores of 50. Before this, a problem seen by only one or two lenses could come first or last on very little evidence: with every lens weighted equally, child deaths came first on two lenses, one of which ranks only two problems. No figure changed, and no problem is removed from the list.
